clue.text: Replace cover and check safe

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
sure means safe, certain, secure

explanation.surface: Someone renews their insurance and makes sure everything is secure.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out insurance again is to renew one's financial protection, replacing the old policy.

clue.text: Nameless seducer stands up to declaim

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
without a name: N, the abbreviation for name, is taken out of the word

parts.note: an enticer lures or tempts, like a seducer

explanation.surface: A seducer, his name withheld, gets up to make a dramatic speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N from ENTICER, leaving ETICER; 'stands up' turns that around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak aloud in a rhetorical way, as when performing a poem from memory.

clue.text: Ignorant and…

parts.note: the clue runs on into the next one, so the phrase means lacking knowledge and, by the continuation, without light, both senses of an idiom of unawareness

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the next clue: the phrase means both 'ignorant' and, taking the next clue's first word, 'benighted', literally without light.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone uninformed, kept from knowledge as if without any light.

clue.text: … benighted, save son first

indicators.note: the son's letter is placed at the front of the charade

parts.note: save in the sense of except is the same as unless

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone ignorant and benighted, except that the son comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted literally means overtaken by night, so without sunshine.

clue.text: Unstable? It's immovable!

definitions.meaning: wobbly or shaky, as a relationship or a table can be
read playfully as 'like a rock', firm and unshakeable

explanation.walkthrough: The same word has opposite senses: shaky, and, as a pun, rock-like and so immovable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and wobbly is one everyday sense; solid as stone is the punning other.

clue.text: Reckless plan staff-officer introduced

indicators.note: brought into the middle of the other word, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer on a general's staff

explanation.surface: A rash scheme into which a staff officer has been brought.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes wild, impulsive behaviour, synonymous with rash.

clue.text: Gossip given added weight by rearrangement

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about a person
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Gossip gains extra weight when it is rearranged in the retelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by reordering the letters of another is exactly this kind of shuffle.

clue.text: Harsh noise causing local annoyance — neighbours, grumbling, put their heads together

indicators.note: the heads, i.e. opening letters, of these five words are joined up

explanation.surface: Neighbours grumble and confer about a din that is bothering the locality.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud metallic ringing sound, unpleasant to the ear.

clue.text: Sorry to have to confine individual to part of camp

parts.note: to pen is to shut in or confine
I, the Roman numeral one, for a single individual
a tent is one unit of a campsite

explanation.surface: An apology for having to keep someone shut in part of a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitent means feeling regret for wrongdoing, i.e. remorseful.

clue.text: One member accepted count corruptly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP, Member of Parliament
U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage
to count on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A politician took a bribe and counted the money dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'accepted' comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' distinction in British usage between upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impurely means acting in a tainted, dishonest way.

clue.text: Creative accounting made a supply that's abundant…

indicators.note: creative accounting suggests the figures are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fiddled books produced a plentiful supply of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creative accounting' looks like one phrase, but 'Creative' alone is the anagram signal and ACCOUNTING MADE A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a plentiful source you can keep going back to for more.

clue.text: …yet herb is wasted because of that

indicators.note: squandered or ruined, so these letters are spoilt and reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing on: and yet the herb is thrown away as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means, as a consequence.

clue.text: Just a piano

definitions.meaning: a type of piano with vertical strings, as opposed to a grand

explanation.definitionFit: An honourable person is described this way; a vertical-cased instrument has the same name.

clue.text: Service area makes a killing

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A service-station area brings in a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a killing' suggests profit; here 'killing' is literal slaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is a slaughter of many people, a mass killing.

clue.text: Lector is employed in a convent

indicators.note: put to use in a different arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader of lessons has a job at a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister, a covered walkway in a religious house, stands for the monastic house itself.

clue.text: Brother shared responsibility for boundary

definitions.meaning: a fellow member of the Freemasons calls another brother
Charles ... surveyed, with Jeremiah Dixon, the line dividing Pennsylvania and Maryland

explanation.walkthrough: The Mason–Dixon line, an 18th-century US boundary, was surveyed by two men, so one of them shared the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason is a lodge brother; the surveyor's surname is the same.

clue.text: Pay for 21 to go off duty

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it
the bird's covering in 21-down, here soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Wages for a worker who is clocking off.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to another clue's answer, a bird's feathers; soft feathers are called down.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to relax from duty, as soldiers do when dismissed.

clue.text: Ran second, and made an impression

parts.note: printing makes an impression on paper

explanation.surface: A runner came second and still impressed people.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint is to run at full speed, so the past tense is a kind of running.

clue.text: Game is part of companion set

definitions.meaning: a card game played for stakes
a fireside companion set holds tongs, brush, shovel and an iron rod for stirring coals

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a gambling card game and the iron for stirring a fire.

clue.text: Noisy bat above your head

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits higher than the second

parts.note: a racket is a bat for tennis or squash

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A loud bat flies over someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackety means making a lot of clattering noise.

clue.text: Ancient Greek mountain-dweller — possibly heartless Polyhymnia

indicators.note: a hint that what remains may be rearranged into another form
the middle of the muse's name is cut out

explanation.surface: A god of the Greek mountain home might be the muse Polyhymnia, minus her heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes HY, the middle of POLYHYMNIA, leaving POLYMNIA; 'possibly' rearranges it. Polyhymnia, muse of sacred song, was herself one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympian gods lived on Mount Olympus, the Greek mountain.

clue.text: Mature tree first provides cover for bird

indicators.note: the tree's word comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: An old tree gives shelter to a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers collectively cover its body.

clue.text: Rude, not sweet, little boy

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
Al is a short form of a boy's name such as Alan

explanation.surface: A small boy is cheeky and not at all sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal means harsh and coarse, a rough sense of rude.

clue.text: Exponents of note in S.E. Asia

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the East Indies are the islands of South-East Asia
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Musicians who champion a note heard in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponents' suggests performers; here it is the maths sense, powers.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths the powers to which a number is raised are also called indices.

clue.text: Greek Ambassador I consider partly responsible for it

indicators.note: the run of words is only partly involved, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: A Greek diplomat is held partly to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is an ancient Greek dialect and architectural order.

clue.text: Ill-bred person in a jumper

definitions.meaning: a cad or rotter, an old-fashioned British term of disapproval
something that bounds, like a kangaroo

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater, but it means one who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is called this; anything that bounds or leaps also fits.

clue.text: Child I found in a store

indicators.note: located inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing crops

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a child hidden in a storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is Scottish and northern English for a youngster.

clue.text: Novel entry for coxed pairs

parts.note: a coxed pair is two rowers plus a cox, so a trio of people in one craft, also the title of Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel

explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic book follows a trio rowing up the Thames, as in a coxed pair.

clue.text: City in the course of time gradually declines

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: days stand for the passing of time
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Over time a city slowly falls into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the City, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To decay is to rot or deteriorate slowly.

clue.text: One lantern broken by domestic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: smashed, so the letters are reformed in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single lantern smashed by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic' looks like a household servant, but it means home as opposed to foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal affairs are home affairs, the opposite of foreign.
